analysis.title: Year Ahead 2027: Sustaining resilience
key_insights: UBS CIO base case for 2027 is 'Resilience, sustained' (50% probability): trend-rate growth, solid earnings, continued AI investment, easing inflation, and a more balanced risk-reward for global equities after strong gains.

The four questions that decide whether resilience holds are: whether AI justifies investor enthusiasm, whether inflation and rates are in a structurally different regime, whether government debt can keep rising without a market reckoning, and whether economics will keep outweighing geopolitics.

Global AI-related investment is on track for USD 1.0tr in 2026, double 2025. UBS forecasts USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028, versus consensus capex of USD 1.6tr in 2027 and USD 1.8tr in 2028. About 80% of forecast 2027 spending comes from Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and SpaceX.

Evidence supporting AI demand: major cloud providers report USD 2.5tr of contracted orders not yet recognized as revenue (about six times latest 12-month cloud revenue), GPU hourly prices remain above their level at DeepSeek's January 2025 launch, hyperscaler cloud revenue grew 57% y/y in 3Q26 (four straight quarters of acceleration), and token costs have more than halved since May while usage rose sixfold.

AI risks named: higher financing and execution risk, surging neocloud borrowing costs, permitting constraints, persistent power shortages, complex financing relationships that may obscure end demand, and open-source or low-cost models compressing supplier pricing power.

UBS would turn concerned on AI investment if capacity expansion outstrips demand growth, AI lab revenue growth slows meaningfully, cloud utilization weakens, or falling AI costs fail to stimulate enough new usage. It would also reassess if algorithmic efficiency sharply cuts compute needs.

Inflation: UBS expects US average inflation of 2.3% in 2027 (3.4% in 2026), Eurozone 3.1% (3.1%), and global 3.4% (3.8%). US services inflation fell from 7.3% y/y in early 2023 to 3.1% in September, and wage growth from 5.9% in March 2022 to 3.1% in October.

Several central banks may tighten further in late 2026 or early 2027 before the hiking cycle ends. UBS expects bond yields to decline modestly later in 2027 but real rates to stay above pre-pandemic norms because of investment, fiscal deficits and debt supply.
Inflation regime would look structurally higher if wage growth reaccelerates, second-round effects from supply shocks appear, or central banks show reduced willingness to return inflation to target.

Government debt: UBS sees rising fiscal strain but no universal tipping point. Long-dated yields are at multi-decade highs while credit risk premiums stay subdued. The UK's long average maturity limits refinancing needs and Germany's debt servicing burden is well below peers.

UBS would worry about a debt crisis if bond auctions became hard to cover with materially higher yields demanded, if fiscal authorities lack the political capacity to stabilize debt, if central banks appear unwilling or unable to respond to stress, or if sovereign stress spreads into banks or credit.

Geopolitics: the Strait of Hormuz closure pushed oil up 52% year to date in 2026. UBS expects the Middle East and Ukraine wars to persist, with US-China tech competition continuing, and expects geopolitics to cause periodic volatility without displacing economics as the main return driver. The S&P 500 has recovered from the average geopolitical shock in 16 days.

Equities: UBS moved global equities, US equities, and Asia ex-Japan and EM equities to Neutral. It prefers the Eurozone (15% 2027 earnings growth, matching the US, from lower valuation and less AI dependence) and favors industrials and health care to diversify away from technology.

Earnings forecasts: S&P 500 earnings up 29% in 2026 and about 15% in 2027, Eurozone about 15%, MSCI Asia ex-Japan 20%. The 10 largest companies are about 40% of the S&P 500, so revisions to a few forecasts have outsized index impact.

Technology positioning: favor financially strong hyperscalers with visible monetization and internally funded investment, plus select leaders in compute, foundry and semiconductor equipment. Be cautious on lower-quality suppliers, leveraged capacity providers and recent bottleneck beneficiaries reliant on continued price increases.

Fixed income rated Attractive: prefer intermediate duration (maturities of about 2 to 10 years), add quality bonds, and favor EM and high yield on a relative basis. EM sovereign yields about 7.1%, EM corporate 7.0%, US high yield about 8.3%. US high yield defaults are expected to stay around 2%, with about 60% of the market rated BB and about 3% maturing within a year.

Gold: maintain long-term exposure and add on pullbacks below USD 4,000/oz. High US real yields and a firm dollar could push gold below USD 4,000 in the short run, but structural buyers are expected to support that level. Forecast is USD 4,600 by June 2027 and USD 5,000 by December 2027.

Copper is the preferred industrial metal, with a forecast of USD 15,500/tonne by end-2027 on grid, data center and electrification demand and slow supply response. UBS projects USD 32tr of global electrical infrastructure spending over the next decade.

Currencies: favor GBP as the preferred G10 carry trade (4.0% BoE policy rate, another hike expected in early 2027), add diversified EM carry (MXN, ZAR, BRL, INR), and use CHF as a funding currency, expecting it to underperform on total return. The USD outlook is balanced.

Volatility strategies: index-level implied volatility is subdued while single-stock volatility is high. UBS favors capital preservation structures, structured yield strategies that monetize single-stock premium, and predefined-entry strategies to build equity exposure, with diversified underlyings and staggered maturities.

Alternatives: favor low-net and market-neutral hedge funds, merger arbitrage, operationally focused private equity and secondaries (volumes up about 15% y/y in 1H), and core and core-plus infrastructure. Private debt is Neutral given tight spreads and rising credit stress.

Scenario probabilities and December 2027 targets: Resilience sustained 50% (S&P 500 8,200, UST 10y 4.75%, Fed 4.50%); Goldilocks 20% (9,500, 4.00%, 4.00%); Yield reset 10% (7,000, 5.50%, 5.25%); AI bust 20% (5,500, 3.00%, 2.00%).
Spot levels as of 12 November 2026: S&P 500 7,592, UST 10y 5.13%, Fed upper bound 4.00%, Brent USD 96, WTI USD 89, gold USD 3,885, copper USD 13,642, EURUSD 1.11, USDJPY 160.

sector_views.rationale: Automation, defense, transport infrastructure, power networks and electrification support earnings. UBS prefers diversified end-market exposure over businesses dependent on data center construction.
Medical innovation, obesity treatments, diagnostics and medtech support revenues, and earnings are less tied to corporate investment. MSCI AC World Health care is up 10% in 2026.

Retain AI exposure but cut concentration. Favor strong hyperscalers and select compute, foundry and semiconductor equipment leaders, and stay cautious on lower-quality suppliers and leveraged capacity providers.
Selective participation where supply constraints are tightest. Electricity demand net of efficiency is rising for the first time in decades, but valuations are high and projects may be delayed.
Favored within Asia for income, rate normalization and balance sheet strength.

earnings_insights: UBS forecast (not reported): S&P 500 EPS growth of about 29% in 2026 and about 15% in 2027, from a house estimate dated 12 November 2026.
UBS forecast: Eurozone EPS growth of about 15% in 2027, MSCI Asia ex-Japan about 20%.
Hyperscaler cloud revenues grew 57% y/y in 3Q26, the fourth consecutive quarter of acceleration (reported figure cited by UBS).
Private equity: the median buyout company delivered 7% revenue growth and 9% EBITDA growth in 2Q (reported, cited by UBS).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Resilient growth around trend supports the base case.
Trend growth in the US supports earnings.
Energy effects fade and inflation moves toward target.
Inflation stays elevated through 2027 before easing in 2028.
Down from 7.3% in early 2023, evidence of disinflation.
Down from 5.9% in March 2022, lowering wage-price spiral risk.
Fed upper bound is 4.00% today, with a UBS forecast of 4.50% by June 2027.
Modest decline in yields as inflation moderates, but structurally higher real rates.
The Strait of Hormuz closure drove the move and pushed refined-product prices higher.

trade_ideas.description: Long GBP versus CHF, EUR and JPY as the preferred G10 carry trade, funding with Swiss francs
trade_ideas.rationale: UK 4.0% policy rate with another hike expected in early 2027 gives sterling a large yield advantage and low volatility supports carry.
trade_ideas.risk: Fiscal credibility in the UK, and a risk-off move reviving safe-haven demand for CHF.

trade_ideas.description: Diversified EM currency carry: Mexican peso, South African rand, Brazilian real, Indian rupee
trade_ideas.rationale: High nominal yields, cautious central banks and contained volatility.
trade_ideas.risk: External balances, political credibility, energy exposure and changing rate differentials.

trade_ideas.description: Add gold on pullbacks below USD 4,000/oz
trade_ideas.rationale: Structural buyers expected to support that level, with real yields easing as markets scale back Fed tightening expectations.
trade_ideas.risk: High US real yields and a firm dollar could push gold lower in the short run.

trade_ideas.description: Build copper exposure during periods of weakness
trade_ideas.rationale: Power grid, data center and electrification demand against slow supply response, with a USD 15,500/tonne end-2027 forecast.
trade_ideas.risk: Sensitivity to Chinese activity, manufacturing, inventories, trade policy and substitution.

trade_ideas.description: Replace part of the equity allocation with capital preservation structures that limit downside while keeping some upside
trade_ideas.rationale: Subdued index implied volatility lowers option costs and higher short-dated yields make the bond component cheaper.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower upside participation, early sale losses, and issuer credit risk.

trade_ideas.description: Equal-weight equity strategies to reduce megacap concentration
trade_ideas.rationale: The 10 largest companies are about 40% of the S&P 500.

risk_factors: AI investment fails to deliver sufficient productivity and earnings gains, or capacity outstrips demand, leading to the 'AI bust' scenario.
Persistent inflation or a renewed energy shock forces further central bank hikes (the 'yield reset' scenario).
Debt refinancing at higher yields, difficult bond auctions, and weaker central bank support raise sovereign stress.
Escalation in the Middle East or Ukraine disrupts energy supply, shipping and inflation.
US-China restrictions on semiconductors, critical minerals and rare earths raise costs and disrupt supply chains.
AI financing relationships may obscure end demand and increase systemic fragility.
Market concentration: the 10 largest companies are about 40% of the S&P 500.
Power, transmission and data center shortages may delay AI deployment and monetization.
vol_and_positioning: Index-level implied volatility is subdued while single-stock volatility is elevated, which UBS says lowers option costs for capital preservation structures and raises single-stock premiums for yield strategies.
Cboe S&P 500 Dispersion Index has risen, supporting stock selection and low-net or market-neutral hedge fund strategies.
The 10 largest companies are about 40% of the S&P 500, concentrating index sensitivity to earnings disappointment.
Currency volatility is low versus its 30-year average, which supports carry strategies.

Structured strategies named: capital preservation (limits downside and upside), structured yield (conditional coupons, capped returns), and predefined-entry (sell downside optionality to build exposure at set levels).
geopolitical: Closure of the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil up 52% year to date in 2026.
Difficult US-Iran negotiations make a settlement unlikely near term, with further US escalation a risk.
The Ukraine war is expected to continue into 2027, supporting European defense and infrastructure spending and limiting additional Russian energy supplies.
US-China competition continues over technology, semiconductors, critical minerals and AI infrastructure.
Democratic control of Congress should support Kyiv and constrain rapprochement with Moscow.

tension_points.bull_case: A flywheel of falling inference costs, rising adoption and investment. Cloud revenue grew 57% y/y in 3Q26, contracted orders are USD 2.5tr, and token usage is up sixfold while costs halved.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex outpaces returns, cloud growth slows or open-source models compress supplier pricing power. Financing relationships may obscure end demand and power shortages may delay monetization.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capacity expansion outstripping demand growth, meaningfully slower AI lab revenue growth, weaker cloud utilization, or falling AI costs failing to stimulate enough new usage.

tension_points.bull_case: Inflation is moderating as shocks fade, services inflation is 3.1%, wage growth is 3.1%, and AI and automation could lower costs.
tension_points.bear_case: Defense, infrastructure, AI and energy security spending plus larger deficits keep real rates structurally higher, and de-globalization raises costs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Wage growth reaccelerating, second-round effects from supply shocks, or central banks showing reduced willingness to return inflation to target.

tension_points.bull_case: Debt ratios can stabilize if nominal growth exceeds funding costs, and governments retain tools such as buybacks, adjusted issuance and domestic ownership incentives.
tension_points.bear_case: Refinancing at higher yields raises debt servicing, and central banks are unlikely to absorb supply through large purchases.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Difficult bond auctions with materially higher yields demanded, political incapacity to stabilize debt, or sovereign stress spreading to banks and credit markets.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets have absorbed shocks, with the S&P 500 recovering from the average geopolitical shock in 16 days, and supply chains and energy markets have adapted.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy disruption in Russia or the Middle East and US-China restrictions on semiconductors and rare earths could cause lasting economic damage.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Sustained disruption to Middle Eastern shipping or Gulf infrastructure, material disruption to energy supply from the Ukraine war, or changes in Western support altering the military balance.
